options.filename: The 5 Storey Pagoda at Kofukuji Temple.jpg
options.author: Ray in Manila
options.description:
Kofukuji used to be the family temple of the Fujiwara, the most powerful family clan during much of the Nara and Heian Periods. The temple was established in Nara at the same time as the capital in 710. At the height of Fujiwara power, the temple consisted of over 150 buildings.
 Today a couple of buildings of great historic value remain, including a five story pagoda and a three story pagoda. At 50 meters, the five story pagoda is Japan's second tallest, just seven meters shorter than the five story pagoda at Kyoto's Toji Temple. Kofukuji's pagoda is both a landmark and symbol of Nara. It was first built in 730, and was most recently rebuilt in 1426.
 
www.japan-guide.com/e/e4101.html

options.filename: Riding the tram (streetcar) to the Atom Bomb Dome (49495761827).jpg
options.author: shankar s.  from Poona (pune), India, India
options.description: Riding the Hiroden tram (streetcar) to the Atom Bomb Dome (acually the Peace Memorial Park) in Hiroshima, Japan. The streetcars were pretty well patronized though most passengers appeared to be short hop passengers. I know because after this ride, I took a pretty long hour and a half ride by tram to Miyajima Guchi ferry terminal- was a constant flow of passengers getting on and off the tram all the time, some riding only for a few stops. You get in from the middle entrance and get off from the front. I got off from the middle door as well, as I was sitting right opposite it, but the crew did not object at all, as long as I swiped my card. The conductor here is seen making an announcement as we near our stop. (Hiroshima,Japan, Apr/ May 2019)
options.credit: Riding the tram (streetcar) to the Atom Bomb Dome

options.filename: This tram (streetcar) isn't going anywhere soon (49495507026).jpg
options.author: shankar s.  from Poona (pune), India, India
options.description: This is the kind of tram (streetcar) I got on my long ride from the atom bomb dome in the Peace Memorial Park in Hiroshima to the Miyajima Guchi ferry terminal- a good hour and a half away. Details of the tram (streetcar) system in Hiroshima appeared earlier in this album. (see previous pictures). The local tram (streetcar) system in Hiroshima is called Hiroden. This particular tram (streetcar) is not going anywhere soon, as the Not in Service sign on it indicates. It's clever of them to change the route number to 0 as well when the tram is not in operation. (Hiroshima,Japan, Apr/ May 2019)
options.credit: This tram (streetcar) isn't going anywhere soon

options.filename: An old tram (streetcar) complete with trolley pole in pre atom bomb Hiroshima (49495685202).jpg
options.author: shankar s.  from Poona (pune), India, India
options.description: Hiroshima in happier times- picture 3 of 5: An old tram (streetcar) complete with trolley pole in pre atom bomb Hiroshima. Hiroshima still has an extensive tram (streetcar) system in operation today, called the Hirodem. As of 2015, two of the older cars which survived the atom bomb were still in operation, though I did not spot them when I visited Hiroshima in 2016. Detailed notes about the USA's atom bomb attack over Hiroshima and other details appeared earlier in this album. (see previous pictures) (Hiroshima,Japan, Apr/ May 2019)
options.credit: An old tram (streetcar) complete with trolley pole in pre atom bomb Hiroshima

options.filename: Sonnenberg Gardens, Canandaigua, New York - 20210820 - 13 - Japanese Garden ornamentation.jpg
options.author: Andre Carrotflower
options.description: An ornamental stone pagoda tower and lantern stand in the Japanese Garden at Sonnenberg Gardens State Historic Park, as seen in August 2020. Formerly an apple orchard, the Japanese Garden was the brainchild of the lady of the house, Mary Clark Thompson, who had seen such a garden on a 1903 trip to Kyoto. Three years later, she hired Japanese-born landscape designer Kikujiro Wadamori to replicate it for her in a style that evoked the landscape of Japan with its hills, lakes and islands. Wadamori and his team of workers completed the garden in only six months.
